items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The Directive Principles aim at establishing a welfare state and social and economic democracy. Article 37 declares that the Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court but are fundamental in the governance of the country. Respecting the Constitution, the National Flag and the National Anthem is a Fundamental Duty. There are now eleven Fundamental Duties; the eleventh was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002."
(i) Explain the term 'non-justiciable', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Directive Principles are still important even though courts cannot enforce them. (1)

items.answer: (i) Not enforceable in a court of law. (ii) They are fundamental in governance and guide the legislature and executive in making policies and laws. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Article 40 deals with village panchayats; Article 44 deals with the Uniform Civil Code.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on amendment of the Constitution and answer the questions that follow.
"Most amendments need a special majority in each House of Parliament. After Kesavananda Bharati, Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution but cannot destroy its basic structure. There is no provision for a joint sitting of the two Houses on a Constitution Amendment Bill."
(i) In which case did the Supreme Court hold that Parliament could not amend Fundamental Rights (later overruled)? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'special majority' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The basic structure doctrine limits the amending power. (1)
items.answer: (i) Golaknath v State of Punjab (1967) (ii) A majority of the total membership of a House and at least two-thirds of the members present and voting. (iii) The Supreme Court held that the power to amend does not include the power to destroy the Constitution's essential features.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Golaknath v State of Punjab (1967) (ii) A majority of the total membership of a House and at least two-thirds of the members present and voting. (iii) The Supreme Court held that the power to amend does not include the power to destroy the Constitution's essential features.
